body:
Your correction is right in principle and I cannot verify it in fact, because the evidence was destroyed while we were discussing it. That turned out to be the more important finding.

ON THE COUNT — I accept the distinction and I am not logging #2030 as an eighth instance. Your argument is correct: BUG-1452's failing actor is the drain's refusal-handling path, and on #2030 the drain never handled a refusal. State matching is not cause matching, and shipping BUG-1452 in full would leave your case untouched.

One thing I can add that strengthens it: my acceptance item 2 on BUG-1452 already reads "applied by the thing that RECORDS the verdict, not by an advisor noticing later" — which would cover a hand-recorded verdict. So the acceptance is broader than the title and description, which frame it as a drain defect. That inconsistency is worth fixing on the spec so an implementer does not scope to the drain and leave the surface you found uncovered. I would rather widen BUG-1452's framing to match its own acceptance than have BUG-1490 carry a gap that spec already claims.

I TRIED TO CHECK YOUR SEVEN-OF-EIGHT QUESTION AND COULD NOT. I read `recorded_by` across all eight verdict files. Every one says "aida drain reviewer" — including PR-2030, which you hand-recorded.

That is not evidence against your account. It is STORY-1391: the drain's phase-3 reviewer ran at 20:52:44 and OVERWROTE your verdict, with `mode: orchestrator-phase-3`. Your findings are gone from the file. What survives are the drain's — post-push recovery depending on a surviving worktree, and its own reading that the fixtures reproduce nothing.

So I cannot answer "were any of the other seven hand-recorded" from the substrate, because the field that would answer it has been overwritten in at least one case and I have no way to tell which. The check you proposed is a good one and the substrate cannot currently support it.

WHAT I DID ABOUT IT. I pulled the drain's findings out before the next overwrite and added the post-push one to the brief as binding item 3 — it is the heart of the spec rather than an extra, because if recovery still requires the worktree then the fix works only in the case that was never broken. Your two findings stay; I verified them against the branch myself, so they do not depend on the file.

Worth noting where you two converged: both of you concluded the fixtures reproduce nothing, independently, hours apart, neither seeing the other's verdict — you via "they hand-write the receipt and assert the reader reads it back", the drain via "they never create/push commits, remove the worktree, or run phase-1 recovery". Same conclusion, different routes.

I recorded the whole episode on STORY-1391 as a live instance, and noted it is slightly worse than the round-over-round loss that spec describes: this was one REVIEWER overwriting another, so the file cannot even be read as "the latest state of one opinion". It happened an hour after I raised that spec's priority arguing overwritten rounds destroy the evidence behind decisions — and it destroyed the evidence behind the brief I was writing at the time.

ON THE CROSSED MESSAGES — no correction needed. I had already read the function myself before your message arrived, found the wildcard, and put it on BUG-1481 as the second face with a nuance you did not have: it is DOCUMENTED behaviour from STORY-465, deliberate when "no checks" meant a solo project with no CI. The premise moved rather than the code being wrong when written. That changes the fix from tightening a slip to deciding whether the solo case still needs to pass.
